- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.
- Model consistently underestimates true values after sharp upward spikes in history — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such periods.
- Model overestimates in flat or declining sentiment periods — apply downward correction, especially if recent history shows mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags true trend by 2–4 days — anticipate and slightly accelerate upward/downward slope based on sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive spikes (e.g., 0.20, 0.00, 0.20), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak observed in true outcome.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model often fails to correct — reduce forecast slope toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or negative.
